frameworks.name: Three-to-Five Year Horizon Planning
frameworks.definition: A decision framework in which individuals plan for outcomes 3–5 years forward, anchored to personal financial stability (resolution of immediate bills and personal constraints) before extending vision further.

frameworks.name: Wealth Progression Milestones and Vision Expansion
frameworks.definition: As revenue crosses capability thresholds ($100k → $300k → $1M), founder skill inventory and market clarity increase, reframing the competitive landscape and revealing previously invisible opportunities.

claims.text: The person with the longest time horizon wins in competitive markets because the remaining arbitrage (alpha) exists only for those willing to wait and endure longer than competitors.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: time horizon is reverse-engineered to reality (not speculative)
bounded_by: Does not apply to commodities or near-zero-differentiation markets where time alone cannot create advantage
Requires alignment of long-term vision to actionable steps; pure waiting without direction fails

claims.text: Alex Hormozi's time horizon is 3–5 years forward; beyond that, he declines to plan because personal circumstances may fundamentally shift. This intermediate horizon allows him to compound action while acknowledging uncertainty beyond the 5-year window.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Shorter horizon (1–2 years) applies to early-stage founders with insufficient capital buffer
Longer horizon (10+ years) applies to capital-intensive infrastructure businesses (Elon Musk's SpaceX / Tesla model)

claims.text: Elon Musk is the richest person in the world because he maintained a childhood ambition (building rockets, electric cars, space exploration) as a coherent time horizon from age 7 onward, demonstrating conviction that outlasted market skepticism and capital constraints.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder with capital access and technical capability
claims.mechanism: A stable long-term vision, once publicly articulated and maintained under rejection, compounds credibility and attracts capital/talent aligned to that vision.
bounded_by: Does not apply to idea-stage founders or those without execution infrastructure
Wealth outcome (billionaire status) is outcome, not mechanism; mechanism is the consistency + capital + execution over decades

claims.text: It is very difficult to have vision when bills require immediate payment; founders must resolve personal financial stability first before their cognitive capacity expands to longer-term strategic thinking.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: personal debt or recurring financial pressure
claims.mechanism: Scarcity (immediate financial stress) consumes working memory and decision-making bandwidth, reducing the available cognitive capacity for long-horizon vision.
bounded_by: Does not apply to founders with external capital (investor funding, family wealth) that eliminates immediate survival pressure
Applies primarily to bootstrapped founders or those with zero external funding

claims.text: The progression from $100k to $1M revenue in a single year is achievable and serves as the critical financial threshold unlocking vision expansion; below this, focus remains on unit economics rather than strategy.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: execution capability to scale sales or delivery
bounded_by: Assumes business model already generates positive unit economics at scale
Timeline (1 year) is possible but not guaranteed; depends on market fit and founder execution velocity

claims.text: When founders cross revenue milestones ($100k → $300k → $1M), their cognitive model of how the market operates shifts; previously invisible competitive opportunities become visible, and their ability to predict outcomes improves.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Accumulated market feedback (customer behavior, pricing response, competitive reactions) updates the founder's predictive model; wealth creation correlates with superior prediction accuracy, not luck.
bounded_by: Does not apply to founders who repeat the same activities without learning from market feedback
Does not apply to passive income or inherited wealth scenarios

claims.text: Entrepreneurs who have practiced the same strategy for extended time without achieving desired outcomes are usually seeing distorted versions of reality rather than reality itself; their misalignment stems from false perception, not poor execution.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: entrepreneur with >2 years in current approach
claims.mechanism: Confirmation bias and limited feedback loops cause entrepreneurs to hold inaccurate mental models of market dynamics; reality check requires external perspective or market-forced recalibration.
bounded_by: Does not apply to early-stage experimentation (<6 months) where statistical noise is high
May not apply if external market shifts (regulatory, economic) have changed the landscape independent of execution quality

claims.text: High-wealth achievers (across industries) demonstrate superior prediction accuracy of future outcomes compared to lower-wealth peers in the same market, which explains wealth differentials independent of luck or timing.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: competitive market with repeated decision-making cycles
sufficient time horizon (3+ years) for prediction accuracy to compound
bounded_by: Does not apply to zero-sum luck-dependent games (casino, lottery)
Does not isolate for survivorship bias; includes only observed successful wealth generators

claims.text: Entrepreneurship serves as the fastest personal development vehicle because market feedback delivers unfiltered truth about decision quality, whereas social relationships and peers typically withhold critical feedback.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder in competitive or capital-efficient business model
market feedback loop <30 days (e.g., sales, revenue, churn data)
claims.mechanism: Immediate financial consequences of decisions (revenue impact, cash flow consequence) force accurate self-assessment; absence of social softening means feedback arrives unfiltered.
bounded_by: Does not apply to long-cycle businesses (real estate, infrastructure, venture portfolio) where feedback takes 2+ years
Requires founder openness to accurate feedback; defensive founders filter even market feedback

examples.text: Elon Musk expressed interest in electric cars and rockets as a young person (pre-sale of Zip2, his first company). Decades later, his entire business portfolio (Tesla, SpaceX) directly reflects those childhood interests. This consistency of vision across time and through capital-raising cycles, product launches, and market criticism demonstrates how conviction under isolation translates to extreme wealth accumulation.

A founder earning $100k–$300k in annual revenue focuses exclusively on the mechanics of reaching $1M: which sales channels to prioritize, how to optimize delivery, customer acquisition cost relative to lifetime value. Once $1M revenue is achieved, the founder's perspective shifts to larger questions about market structure, competitive moats, and which entire customer segments to pursue—questions invisible at $300k revenue because they lacked the execution data to see them.

practices.text: Founders should resolve personal financial stability (paying bills, eliminating personal debt, establishing a buffer) before attempting to engage in long-horizon strategic thinking.
Focus on achieving $100k–$1M revenue progression as the primary goal; do not diversify attention to multi-year strategic questions until this revenue milestone is reached.

Regularly audit whether current strategies are producing desired outcomes; if outcomes are persistently suboptimal over multiple cycles (6+ months), assume the mental model of market reality is distorted rather than the execution was weak.

Expose yourself to frequent market feedback loops (weekly or daily revenue/sales data, customer churn, win/loss analysis) rather than relying on peer advice or industry convention, to calibrate your mental model to reality.
